description: Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time, checked against the original's recorded behavior at every step. CLIs, HTTP servers and libraries in TypeScript, Python, C, Go, Ruby and Java.

latest_release.name: v4.1.0
latest_release.body:
- `enable --only <fn>` (repeatable) switches on just the named functions of a unit, and `--partial`
  switches on every function whose recorded cases all match, so a unit with many exports can go
  over one function at a time. Running it again widens or narrows the marked block in place (#351, #412 by @Lewandox).
- `report` takes `--resolve-from <dir>` like `bench` and `fuzz`, in the CLI and the MCP tool, for
  repositories whose `node_modules` lives elsewhere (#349, #402 by @XiaoBinGan).
- `analyze`'s Start here details name the sibling a unit imports in the same package, which is what
  puts it in a later wave (#348, #422 by @XiaoBinGan).
- A Kotlin unit that takes or returns `ByteArray`, `ShortArray` or `FloatArray` says that the Java
  wire cannot carry that array type yet, instead of calling it a class (#369, #386 by @XiaoBinGan).

- `bridge --batch` on a C unit, and `refresh --batch` on a C, PHP, C# or PowerShell crate, fail with
  "`--batch` is not available for <language> units yet" instead of saving a batch that generates
  nothing (#434, #440 by @SPD-RYUK).
- Java and Kotlin ports turn `Err("Type: message")` into the same exception on the JSON, typed, wire
  and batch paths, and look in `java.time` and `java.util.concurrent` too, so a typed call no
  longer throws `RuntimeException` for `DateTimeException` (#359, #438 by @SPD-RYUK).
- `report` says "Nx slower" for a port slower than the original in the card's `aria-label` and in
  REPORT.md's speedup rows, instead of "0.0x faster" and `0.0x` (#433, #437 by @draarivpatel-ui).
- `analyze` and `map` count lines of code the way `gate`'s size check does, leaving out comment
  lines, so licence headers and JSDoc no longer move a file's Lines, Start here or priority (#342, #435 by @AyhamJo7).
- `profile` and `go` on a Node that refuses `--cpu-prof` in `NODE_OPTIONS` (22.14) pass it to a `node`
  command as arguments, and stop with a clear message for wrappers such as `npx` (#346, #429 by @AyhamJo7).
- `profile` leaves a script's top level (Python's `<module>`, Node's line-1 module function) out of
  "What to port" and no longer advises porting it with a function it calls in a loop (#344, #428 by @AyhamJo7).
- Java and Kotlin parameters accept covariant wildcards and projections (`List<? extends CharSequence>`,
  `List<out CharSequence>`, `Map<String, ? extends Integer>`, `Array<out String>`) through both the
  reflection converter and the binary wire; return positions, `? super T` and `in T` stay refused (#367, #439 by @Lewandox).
- `app record --effects smtp` records each email as its decoded `From`, `To`, `Cc` and `Subject`
  and its MIME parts (attachments as name, type, size and SHA-256), so the same mail sent with
  different MIME framing matches. `--effects smtp-raw` keeps the raw DATA, and cases recorded
  before this keep replaying against the raw form until recorded again (#333, #426 by @Lewandox).
- Go ports map matching error messages back to the package's exported sentinel errors, so callers using `errors.Is` keep working (#365, #413 by @Lewandox).
- `record --ignore-key-order` saves the choice with the crate, so `gate`, `enable`, `report` and
  `go` compare objects regardless of key order too; `--no-ignore-key-order` undoes it (#352, #409 by @XiaoBinGan).
- `map` gives each unit without a port `analyze`'s status and lists the blocked and kept ones
  with the reason, so they no longer read as work left to port (#350, #421 by @XiaoBinGan).
- On Windows, `profile` and `go` find the project's own functions in a Node workload: Node's
  `file:///C:/...` frame URLs kept the slash before the drive letter, so no frame matched the
  project root and `go` stopped with `no hot function to port` (#407, #408 by @Momentum96).
- `app record` and `app replay` fail with `port <port> is already in use` before spawning a server
  on an occupied port and check whether the child exited before treating the port as ready (#326, #395 by @brixtonpham).
- `Err("Outer+Inner: message")` i

rust-anything

English · Türkçe · Українська · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · Deutsch · Français · Русский · 日本語 · 한국어 · Azərbaycanca · Oʻzbekcha · Қазақша · Кыргызча · Türkmençe · Татарча · ئۇيغۇرچە · Português · Tiếng Việt · Español · Italiano · Bahasa Indonesia · العربية · فارسی · हिन्दी · + add yours

Rewrite your app in Rust, and prove it still behaves the same.
Point it at your app: it records what the original does, your coding agent writes the Rust one piece at a time,
and every piece is checked against that recording before it moves on. It doesn't translate code; it proves the rewrite.

Documentation: https://rust-anything.com/


Install · Releases · Claude Code plugin · MCP Registry · Real-world ports · FAQ
Languages · How it works · Whole apps · Sponsors · MIT
Made in Türkiye 🇹🇷 by erKam Yaman · ❤️ Sponsor me · Sponsored by CodeRabbit

Also by me: safe-anything, a 100% Rust security scanner for code, secrets, configs and AI agent setups. Find the holes before someone else does.

New in 2.0: Prettier, ported to Rust. 19x faster · 15,861 of 17,224 recorded runs fully in Rust · every run byte-identical


Prettier against its Rust port on 59 real files from ms, Fuse.js and json-server (Apple M4). Same output, byte for byte. How it was measured.

PHP and C#: unit ports, through FFI and P/Invoke.

Record
record runs the original on generated edge cases, semantic traps and your own inputs, and saves what it returns or throws. 		Port
bridge generates the Rust crate and a wrapper, so callers keep the original API. You or your agent write the Rust. 		Check
diff replays every recorded case against the Rust, and nothing ships until they all match and gate passes. 		Lift
When replay passes with no fallback and every unit passes gate, app lift makes it a pure Rust app. The original is never touched.
**Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time.** rust-anything records what your Node.js (TypeScript/JavaScript), Python, C, Go, Ruby, Java or Kotlin app does today, then checks every piece of the Rust rewrite against that recording before it moves on, until the app is pure Rust. CLIs, HTTP servers and libraries; your coding agent (or you) writes the Rust. It is built on [napi-rs](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs), [PyO3](https://github.com/PyO3/pyo3) and [wasm-bindgen](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen), which carry the calls between your language and Rust; rust-anything decides what to move and proves it matches. It can only catch what the recording covers: see [What it can't catch](docs/how-it-works.md#what-it-cant-catch). Whole tools and servers, or only the slow part, one hot path at a time: | Real project, same output as the original | Original | With rust-anything | | --- | ---: | ---: | | [Prettier](docs/real-world.md#prettier) 3.6.2, 2,360 JS/TS files from the command line | 128.6 s | **6.9 s: 19x faster** | | Prettier, 6,305 Markdown files from the command line | 352 s | **22.5 s: 15.6x faster** | | [json-server](docs/real-world.md#json-server), a whole Node server: memory at idle | 74 MB | **3.5 MB**, one 5.3 MB binary | | json-server, from start to first response | 79 to 85 ms | **8 to 10 ms** | | [Fuse.js](docs/real-world.md#fusejs) search over 50,000 strings, per query | 91.2 ms | **2.8 ms: 32x faster** | Prettier: 15,861 of 17,224 recorded runs format fully in Rust across 10 languages (JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, JSON, GraphQL, YAML, Markdown, CSS, SCSS, Less), and all 17,224 match Prettier byte for byte, since anything not ported yet falls back to Prettier. json-server: 514/514 recorded HTTP cases match on a pure Rust binary. Measured on an Apple M4, two runs each, every output compared before timing ([details](docs/real-world.md)). Calling Rust once per small function is usually *slower* than a JIT; rust-anything finds the loop worth moving, and moves it. Against C the win is safety, not speed: [ffmpeg's libavutil](docs/real-world.md#ffmpeg) ported to Rust matches all 226,447 recorded calls and runs at about C's speed (18 of 42 benchmarks even, 8 faster, 16 slower by 3 to 40%). ## Only the slow part You don't have to port the whole app. Point `go` at a command that is too slow, and it ports the one function that takes the time: ```sh rust-anything go --agent claude -- python3 app.py ``` It profiles the run, picks the outermost function worth moving (the loop, not the small call inside it, batched where the profile says so), records it on generated inputs plus the calls your run makes, and hands `src/port.rs` to your agent (`claude`, `codex`, or any command that reads a prompt on stdin; without `--agent` it writes `TASK.md` for you and stops). It switches the function on only when every recorded case matches and `gate` passes. Then: ```sh rust-anything report rust/dedupe-rs # REPORT.md and card.svg for the pull request rust-anything disable rust/dedupe-rs # back to the original, byte for byte ``` The [Fuse.js](docs/real-world.md#fusejs) row above is this shape: Fuse's score for one string, batched over the list, moved to Rust while object keys, extended search and the rest stay in JavaScript, for 91.2 ms to 2.8 ms per query over 50,000 strings. Try `go` on [`tests/fixtures/go-fuzzy`](tests/fixtures/go-fuzzy), a 20-line Python dedupe. Every way to switch a port on and off: [Switch a port on and off](docs/how-it-works.md#switch-a-port-on-and-off).


json-server, a whole Node server, lifted to a pure Rust binary (Apple M4). How it was measured.

> rust-anything is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by the Rust Project > or the Rust Foundation. "Rust" is a trademark of the Rust Foundation. > [!WARNING] > `record` and `app record` run your original code, calling each function (or the whole app) on > many generated inputs, and `app record` runs every case twice. `diff`, `gate` and `app replay` > run the same cases again, on the port or the original. Code that writes files, talks to a > database or calls the network does that once per case. Run them on a copy of the project, with a > test database and no production credentials in the environment. ## Install the ports The ESLint port is an npm command. It runs the Rust port for what it covers and ESLint 10.15.0, pinned as a dependency, for everything else, so the output is ESLint's either way: ```sh npm install -g eslint-rs # ESLint 10.15.0 ``` | Command | Answered in Rust | Handed to ESLint 10.15.0 | | --- | --- | --- | | `eslint-rs` | `--no-config-lookup --rule ... --stdin` with the 90 ported rules (`stylish` and `json` output, fixes, suggestions) | `eslint.config.*` lookups (`eslint .`), files and folders, the other 202 core rules, plugins, parsers, the other formatters, parse errors | The binary comes for macOS (arm64, x64) and Linux (x64, arm64, glibc). On Windows and elsewhere, or with `RUST_ANYTHING_MODE=old`, `eslint-rs` runs ESLint itself: same output, no speedup. Installed from its tarballs on macOS arm64, `eslint-rs` matches ESLint 10.15.0 installed beside it on all 10,585 recorded runs ([how](docs/packaging.md#a-whole-cli-front-door)). The Prettier port is packaged the same way (`prettier-rs`, Prettier 3.6.2) and replays 17,224/17,224 recorded runs from its tarballs, 7.9% handed to Prettier, but it is not on npm. `rust-anything package` makes this kind of package from any CLI front door. ## Quick start Paste this into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI or OpenCode and let your agent install it: ```text Install rust-anything: run `cargo install rust-anything`, then `rust-anything setup`. Tell me when to restart you. ``` Or yourself: ```sh cargo install rust-anything # from crates.io rust-anything setup # registers it with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode ``` No Rust toolchain yet? Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows are attached to each [GitHub release](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/releases), and for JavaScript projects `npm install -g rust-anything` installs the same binary. In Claude Code you can also install it as a plugin (the MCP server and the skill; the CLI above must be on your `PATH`): ```text /plugin install rust-anything --marketplace erkamyaman/rust-anything ``` In Codex, from the agents marketplace in this repo (`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, the same plugin under `plugin/`, with the skill and MCP server): ```sh codex plugin marketplace add erkamyaman/rust-anything codex plugin add rust-anything@rust-anything ``` `setup` adds the MCP server to each agent it finds and installs the workflow skill where the agent reads skills. It keeps your other settings, is safe to run again, and `--remove` undoes it. Then ask your agent, for example: - *"Rewrite this CLI in Rust with rust-anything, end to end, and prove it behaves the same."* - *"This search feels slow. Profile it with rust-anything and move the hot loop to Rust."* - *"Plan a migration of `src/parser/` to Rust with rust-anything; port the first unit and prove it."* - *"Bench the Rust port in `rust/text-rs` against the original and tell me whether to ship it."* ### Works with | Agent | `rust-anything setup` adds | | --- | --- | | Claude Code | MCP server in `~/.claude.json`, skill in `~/.claude/skills/` | | Codex | MCP server in `~/.codex/config.toml`, skill in `~/.codex/skills/` | | Cursor | MCP server in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` | | Gemini CLI | MCP server in `~/.gemini/settings.json` | | OpenCode | MCP server in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (`mcp.servers`), skill in `~/.config/opencode/skills/` | | Any other MCP client | add `rust-anything mcp` as a stdio server by hand (see [Install](docs/install.md#install)) | Before changing a file that exists, `setup` saves a copy beside it (`.rust-anything.bak`); `--no-backup` skips the copy. To wire OpenCode up by hand, put the server in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (`command` is the whole argv) and copy [`skills/rust-anything/`](./skills/rust-anything) to `~/.config/opencode/skills/rust-anything/`: ```json { "mcp": { "servers": { "rust-anything": { "type": "local", "command": ["rust-anything", "mcp"] } } } } ``` Or run the steps yourself: ```sh rust-anything profile . -- node bench.mjs # what is hot, and who calls it rust-anything bridge . src/fuzzy.ts --batch fuzzyScore:text # write src/port.rs (or let your agent), then: rust-anything record rust/fuzzy-rs && rust-anything build rust/fuzzy-rs rust-anything diff rust/fuzzy-rs # every recorded case must match rust-anything fuzz rust/fuzzy-rs --time 60 --keep # fresh inputs: what the recording missed rust-anything bench rust/fuzzy-rs # faster? the verdict says rust-anything gate rust/fuzzy-rs # done means this passes ``` rust-anything does not translate code: your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, ...) or you write the Rust. rust-anything supplies what an agent cannot guess reliably: where the time goes, what to port first and in which order, a bridge so the rest of the code calls the Rust with its API unchanged, the exact behavior the port must match, a safe way to ship it, and a gate that says when a port is done. Same output is not enough. Record what the app sends too, and a rewrite that mails twice fails:


A real run of app record --effects and app replay. See Side effects.

## Languages | Language | Unit | Bridge | Recorded and replayed by | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TypeScript/JavaScript | folder or file | napi-rs or wasm-bindgen with a generated binary wire; classes and async included | Node, running the `.ts` sources | | Python | package or module | PyO3 (abi3), direct conversion, typed exceptions | Python, importing the original | | C | `.c` file | `extern "C"` functions with the original names and a header | the original compiled to a shared library, called through ctypes, one fork per case | | Go | package | typed cgo calls and a generated binary wire, in a package with the original API | a generated Go driver, built as its own module | | Ruby | file or folder of module functions | a magnus extension under the original modules | a generated Ruby driver | | Java | package of `public static` methods | typed JNI and a generated binary wire, in wrapper classes with the original methods | a generated reflection driver | | Kotlin | Gradle module of top-level functions and `@JvmStatic` methods | the Java bridge: typed JNI in Java wrapper classes calling the compiled Kotlin statics | a generated reflection driver, with the Kotlin sources compiled by `kotlinc` | | PHP | file or folder of top-level functions (`public static` methods stay in PHP) | a JSON dispatcher over `ext-ffi`, in a file that redeclares the functions with the original parameters | a generated PHP driver; whole apps with `app record`, `app replay` and the front door, for CLIs and servers (`php -S`) | | PowerShell | `.psm1` module or `.ps1` script of functions with `param()` blocks (exported per `Export-ModuleMember`) | a JSON dispatcher over P/Invoke, declared at load time with Reflection.Emit, in a `.ps1` that redeclares each function with its original `param()` block | a generated `pwsh` driver (PowerShell 7.4+) | | C# | file or folder of `public static` methods | a JSON dispatcher over P/Invoke, in `.Rust` classes with the original methods | a generated reflection driver, compiled with the project's sources by `dotnet build`; whole apps with `app record`, `app replay` and the front door, for CLIs and ASP.NET servers (`dotnet .dll`) | Every language except C, PHP, C# and PowerShell also gets batch classes (`--batch`): the items cross once and stay in Rust, and each call runs over all of them on all cores. The language is detected from the repository (`go.mod`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`/`build.gradle.kts`, a `.csproj` or `.sln`, `pyproject.toml`, `Gemfile`, `composer.json`, `package.json`, else the most common source files); a Gradle module with `.kt` sources and no `.java` sources is Kotlin, mixed modules stay Java. `--lang` overrides it. Types come from the source: TS types, Python hints, C, Go, Java, Kotlin and C# signatures, Ruby YARD tags, PHP types and phpdoc; untyped parameters used as numbers are inferred as numbers. For Android, `rust-anything build --profile android` builds the same JNI library with the NDK for `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a` and `x86_64` (or the `--abi` values you pass) and installs it into `/jniLibs//`; `--api` sets the API level (minimum 26, which the generated Java runtime needs). It finds the NDK from `ANDROID_NDK_HOME`/`ANDROID_NDK_ROOT` or the SDK, needs the Rust targets (`rustup target add aarch64-linux-android armv7-linux-androideabi x86_64-linux-android`), links 64-bit libraries with 16 KB page alignment, and checks that every JNI entry point is exported. Gradle looks in `src/main/jniLibs` by default, so pass `--jni-libs app/src/main/jniLibs` or add `/jniLibs` to `sourceSets.main.jniLibs.srcDirs`. `rust-anything record --profile android` runs the original Kotlin unit under ART on a connected device (adb), dexes the generated driver with `d8` from the SDK's build-tools, and pulls the results back as the same `cases.jsonl`; `diff --profile android` replays them against the `.so` built for the device's ABI. Both need `adb`, a device, `kotlinc`, an SDK with build-tools and a platform, and `--device ` when more than one device is connected. The profile covers logic units: Activity/Compose/XML UI, lifecycle and SDK-only classes stay in Kotlin, and each call crosses JNI, so prefer the generated batch wrappers for hot loops. On a host, `record` and `diff` keep using the desktop JVM. For PHP, `analyze` plans a PHP app (Composer packages and PSR-4 autoloading, risks such as loose comparison and integer overflow into floats, Composer packages mapped to crates), and a PHP CLI or server can be recorded, replayed and put behind a Rust front door. A unit's top-level functions with scalar, string, list and assoc-array parameters are bridged through PHP's FFI extension (`php` with `ext-ffi`, on by default for the CLI): once `diff` passes, require the generated `php/.php` (the name is the crate with `-` written as `_`, so `foo-rs` is `php/foo_rs.php`) where the app required the original, and leave both files where they are: the wrapper loads its native library relative to its own folder, so moving it breaks the load. The wrapper declares each bridged function unconditionally, with no `function_exists` guard, so it replaces the original file rather than joining it. Whatever else that file holds cannot come along: classes, `public static` methods, functions the bridge keeps in PHP (a `callable` or `Closure` parameter, say), and top-level statements such as `define('FEATURE_ENABLED', true)` are not in the wrapper, and requiring both files redeclares the bridged functions. Keep those in a file that stays required. Each call crosses as JSON, about 1 µs, so `bench` shows small functions slower than PHP; there is no `shadow` for PHP yet ([issue #200](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/issues/200)). C# works the same way: `analyze` reads `.csproj` projects and their NuGet packages (mapped to crates), resolves `using` directives to folders, and flags what C# does differently (`decimal`, `dynamic`, LINQ's deferred queries, `Task`, `lock`, reflection). A C# CLI or ASP.NET server can be recorded, replayed and put behind a Rust front door. A unit's public static methods with scalar, string, array, list, dictionary and record or plain-class parameters are bridged through P/Invoke (`dotnet` on PATH to record and diff): once `diff` passes, compile the generated `cs/` wrapper (one file named after the crate: `foo-rs` gives `cs/FooRs.cs`) into the project and keep the built native library next to the app, then call the generated classes in the `.Rust` namespace (`Acme.Text.Slug.Slugify` becomes `Acme.Text.Rust.Slug.Slugify`), or alias them with `using`. Each call crosses as JSON, about 1-3 µs, so `bench` shows small methods slower than .NET; there is no `shadow` for C# yet ([issue #200](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/issues/200)). For PowerShell, `analyze` reads `.psm1` modules, `.ps1` scripts and `.psd1` manifests (`RequiredModules`), follows `Import-Module`, `using module` and dot-sourced files, and flags what PowerShell does differently: implicit output and array unrolling, case-insensitive `-eq`, `-match` and hashtable keys, `$null`, and implicit conversions (`5 / 2` is 2.5, `[int]2.5` is 2). A unit's functions with `[string]`, integer, `[double]`, `[bool]`/`[switch]`, array, `[hashtable]` or untyped parameters are bridged through P/Invoke from a generated `ps/.ps1`; filters, `begin`/`process` blocks, pipeline input, `[scriptblock]`, `[ref]` and other .NET types stay in PowerShell with the reason. Once `diff` passes, `rust-anything enable ` dot-sources the wrapper at the end of the original file. Each call crosses as JSON encoded by PowerShell code: about 0.1 ms for a few scalars on an Apple M4, more for arrays and hashtables, so only functions that do more work than that per call get faster (`bench` measures it for yours). Most slow PowerShell in tools is the start-up of a new `pwsh` or `powershell.exe` per command (0.24 to 0.45 s for `pwsh -NoProfile -c 1` on the same M4), which no port fixes: keep one shell open and send it the commands (see the [FAQ](docs/faq.md)). ## Learn more - [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md): the loop, what `bridge` and `analyze` decide, hot paths, what it can't catch, what a real port takes, and keeping up with the original (`map`) - [Ship a port as a package](docs/packaging.md): maturin wheels and napi-rs per-platform npm packages, with the CI that builds them - [Port a whole app](docs/whole-apps.md): servers, CLIs and libraries, from the front door to `app lift` - [Examples and case studies](docs/examples.md): x18n, and real code in eight languages - [Real-world ports](docs/real-world.md): json-server, Fuse.js, vercel/ms, with benchmarks - [Install, update and develop](docs/install.md): every install method, Windows, and building from source - [FAQ](docs/faq.md) · [Status](docs/STATUS.md) · [MCP tools](docs/tools.md) ## Sponsors

rust-anything is free and open source. If it helps your work, please consider sponsoring it.
Your support keeps development going.

Your safety comes first: sponsors get a logo and a link here, nothing more. No paid recommendations and no setup guides for third-party AI API resellers, so nothing here steers your code, keys or data somewhere you didn't choose.

## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome; [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) covers the setup, where tests go, and how to add a language. Design choices and their reasons are in [DECISIONS.md](./DECISIONS.md). Case studies of real ports are especially welcome. Please report security problems privately ([SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md)), and see the [code of conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## License [MIT](./LICENSE) © [Erkam Yaman](https://github.com/erkamyaman).
